observations: Torah #120 contains no bechina (parallel aspect / shared nature) statements whatsoever. The teaching is entirely practical/advisory: it discusses kavvanot in prayer, the danger of practicing them unworthily (compared to kishuf), and the primacy of simple word-meaning as the vehicle for devekut. All relationships in this torah are eitza-type (cause-and-effect / practical advice): e.g., praying with kavvanot without worthiness LEADS TO something like kishuf; focusing on perush hamilot (simple meaning) LEADS TO devekut. Since there are no bechina-connected concepts, no packages can be formed — neither from the existing dataset nor from the source text.
